newsitem.title: INDIA: Major shareholders to review ITC working.
newsitem.headline: Major shareholders to review ITC working.

text.p: Indian financial institutions and B.A.T Industries Plc, major shareholders of India's ITC Ltd, said on Tuesday they would review operations of the tobacco giant at a board meeting scheduled for November 15.
ITC officials have been accused by a federal agency of violation of India's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act involving $100 million.

The decision to review ITC's operations was taken at a joint meeting of financial institutions and B.A.T, the major shareholders, on Tuesday, the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) said in a statement.

IDBI is India's largest financial institution and a major ITC shareholder. B.A.T was represented by Tony Johnston, B.A.T managing director, who was accompanied by B.A.T executives Simon Smith, Timothy Lord and Richard Pilbeam, IDBI said.

The Unit Trust of India, Life Insurance Corp of India, General Insurance Corp of India, Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India and Industrial Finance Corp of India -- other institutional shareholders in ITC -- were also present.
"As major shareholders of ITC, both financial institutions and B.A.T expressed concern over the recent happenings in the company," the statement said.
The financial institutions together hold about 38 percent of ITC's equity while B.A.T has a stake of 31.7 percent.

"Financial institutions on their part reaffirmed that other than what had come in the special audit report and in respect of which the board had taken necessary follow up actions, they had no knowledge of any irregular activities or violation of law by the company or its executives," it said.
"The company has yet to furnish full particulars in respect of some transactions that were recently reported in the press on which the board had asked for full information," it added.

All participants at Tuesday's meeting agreed that pending the findings of the current enquiry by the Enforcement Directorate, it is necessary to have a review of the corporate culture, relationship of ITC with group companies and delegation and internal control mechanisms in the firm.
The participants said it was important to bring the operations of the company to normal level as expeditiously as possible.
It said Johnston had sought an appointment with IDBI chairman in the middle of October.
